title: iGEM Calibration Protocol for Flow Cytometry Cell Size
author: Jacob Beal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5ncg5aw

steps.title: Prepare experimental cell samples
steps.instruction: Culture experimental cells according to your experimental design and prepare them for flow cytometry analysis.

steps.title: Prepare PPS-6K bead calibration sample
steps.instruction: Follow the SpheroTech protocol to prepare the PPS‑6K bead sample for calibration.

steps.title: Measure samples and set detector voltages
steps.instruction: Run all samples on the flow cytometer. Using the bead sample, adjust the FSC channel voltage so the highest bead peak remains below detector saturation. With the negative process control sample, adjust forward‑scatter and side‑scatter voltages to center the strong cell peak in the detector range. Set instrument gating to retain all cell events. Acquire at least 10,000 events for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Adjust FSC voltage with bead sample until top bead peak is below saturation.
Adjust FSC and SSC voltages with negative control to center strong cell peak.
Set gating to keep all cell events.

steps.title: Compute scaling function with TASBE
steps.instruction: Use TASBE Flow Analytics to calculate the Eμm per arbitrary unit scaling function from the bead sample and generate a TASBE color model.

steps.title: Convert data to micrometer units
steps.instruction: Apply the TASBE Flow Analytics analysis functions to convert experimental data from arbitrary units to Eμm.
